title: Gently Fall the Dews of Eve
description: Gently Fall the Dews of Eve in Tonic Solfa to HEINLEIN, doh is F: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 2 verses and a piano.
about: Sarah Flower Adams wrote these words. They were printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion, compiled by Samuel Longfellow and Samuel Johnson (Boston, 1848), as hymn 335, “Dews and Tears”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Sevens (7.7.7.7) (7.7.7.7), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to HEINLEIN; any other Sevens (7.7.7.7) tune fits them as well.
underlay: Gen-tly fall the dews of eve, Rais-ing still the lan-guid flowers; Sweet-ly flow the tears that grieve O'er a mourn-er's strick-en hours.

lines: Gently fall the dews of eve,
Sweetly flow the tears that grieve
Blessed dews and tears that yet
Let us still His praise repeat,
Who in mercy all hath given.

source: A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848)
licence: Public domain: Sarah Flower Adams died in 1848.
credits: Words by Sarah Flower Adams (1805–1848), public domain, as printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848); set to HEINLEIN by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
